CBSE • CLASS 10 • MATHEMATICS

Ch 10 · Circles — Practice

Attempt first, then open the answer. Everything here is original practice material mapped to the current syllabus.

MCQs

The number of tangents from a point on the circle is: (a) 0 (b) 1 (c) 2 (d) infinite

(b) 1.

The angle between a tangent and the radius at the point of contact is: (a) 45° (b) 60° (c) 90° (d) 180°

(c) 90°.

Two tangents from an external point to a circle are: (a) unequal (b) equal (c) always perpendicular (d) parallel

(b) Equal.

Written questions

1 marks How many tangents can be drawn from a point inside a circle?

None. A line through an interior point must cut the circle at two points.

2 marks From a point 13 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm, a tangent is drawn. Find its length.

The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so the three lengths form a right triangle.
Length = √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12 cm.

3 marks Prove that the lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal.

Let P be the external point and PA, PB the tangents with points of contact A and B.
Join OA, OB and OP.
In ΔOAP and ΔOBP: OA = OB (radii), OP is common, and ∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90° (tangent ⊥ radius).
By RHS congruence, ΔOAP ≅ ΔOBP, so PA = PB.

4 marks A quadrilateral ABCD circumscribes a circle. Prove that AB + CD = AD + BC.

Let the tangent segments from A, B, C, D be p, q, r, s respectively.
Then AB = p + q, BC = q + r, CD = r + s and AD = p + s.
AB + CD = p + q + r + s and AD + BC = p + s + q + r.
The two sums are identical, so AB + CD = AD + BC.
